title: cost-optimization: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Context: customers running production workloads saw variable unit economics across models and sequences. This PR introduces sane defaults and automation for batching and prefix/KV caching, ships a set of quantization profiles for common model families, and adds unit-economics tooling to surface estimated cost/latency tradeoffs to the Console and the autotune service. Motivation: reduce onboarding friction for cost-sensitive customers and make automatic recommendations reproducible and auditable.

What this PR does: - Add default batching and caching configuration templates that are applied when a model is onboarded or when a route has no explicit overrides. Defaults are workload-aware and derived from observed latency percentiles. - Introduce quantization profile definitions (int8 and mixed-int8) for Llama-family and MPT-family models plus a conservative profile for other architectures. Profiles include expected RAM/throughput multipliers and fidelity tags. - Wire quant profiles into the model catalog UI and the autotune engine so that recommendations can suggest profile switches when unit-econ improves within a fidelity budget. - Add a lightweight unit-economics tool that consumes traces + model cost metadata to output per-route estimates (tokens, effective batch size, estimated cost-per-1k-tokens, p95 latency). This is surfaced in the Console and available as an internal CLI for SRE/product to run ad-hoc. - Integration tests for the autotune decision flow and end-to-end CI coverage for applying defaults on model onboarding.

Checklist: - [x] Defaults applied via onboarding flow and retroactively on an opt-in migration job - [x] Quant profiles added to catalog and documented - [x] Autotune uses unit-econ delta as a signal to propose profile/queue changes - [x] Console panels for unit-econ estimates added - [x] Integration tests and e2e CI checks added - [x] Migration script for existing routes included

Performance notes: In internal canary runs we saw a median cost reduction of 18% for high-throughput routes (due to more aggressive batching + mixed-int8 profiles) and a 6% regression in p95 latency in worst-case tail scenarios; autotune will avoid profile changes where latency SLOs would be violated.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: quantization may reduce output fidelity in edge cases. Mitigation: profiles are tagged with recommended eval sets and autotune requires at least two eval runs with no regressions before recommending in production. - Risk: autoupdating defaults could cause unexpected behavior for routes with custom tuning. Mitigation: migration is opt-in by default and requires explicit acceptance; routes with explicit overrides are left unchanged.

Related: ENG-4721 (unit-econ model), ENG-4699 (autotune decision engine), SUP-1453 (customer support ticket requesting cost tooling).

feat(catalog): add quantization profiles for llama/mpt/xformer-family
feat(onboarding): apply batching/caching defaults on model onboarding
feat(console): add unit-econ estimates panel and CLI export
chore(tests): add integration tests for default application and autotune decisions
scripts(migration): route-migration tool to opt routes into defaults
review_comments: Priya Natarajan: Can we add a guard to ensure autotune doesn't flip profiles for routes with manual overrides? (response: yes, added explicit check in onboarding/defaults.py)
Diego Morales: Tests look good but can we add a synthetic workload test for tail latency regression? (response: added p95 regression test in e2e_autotune.yml)
Lena Park: Docs need an admin-facing note about migration opt-in and customer communication. (response: expanded docs/ops/unit-econ.md and added migration FAQ)
Priya Natarajan: Are the quant profiles tied to specific kernel availability? (response: profiles include kernel capability tags and autotune checks host kernel list before recommending)
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals from Priya, Diego, Lena. CI green. Migration script will be run against a canary tenant next week.
release_notes: Defaults for batching/caching and quantization profiles added; autotune now considers unit-economics deltas when recommending profile/queue changes. Admins can opt routes into defaults using the migration tool.
notes_for_release_engineering: Run migration/opt_in_migration.py against canary namespace and monitor console unit-econ panel for regressions. Coordinate with SRE to watch p95 latency alerts for 72h.
